candidates.title: The 16-column hydro penalty vocabulary is declared three times inside cobre-core, two of them field-for-field identical

evidence.command:
python3 -c "
import re
g=lambda p,n:(lambda s:re.findall(r'pub (\w+): (\S+?),',s[s.index('pub struct '+n+' {'):s.index('\n}',s.index('pub struct '+n+' {'))]))(open(p).read())
a=g('crates/cobre-core/src/entities/hydro.rs','HydroPenalties')
b=g('crates/cobre-core/src/model/resolved/penalties.rs','HydroStagePenalties')
c=g('crates/cobre-core/src/model/penalty.rs','HydroPenaltyOverrides')
print(len(a),len(b),len(c),a==b,[x for x,_ in a]==[x for x,_ in c])
"
evidence.reading: All three structs declare exactly 16 fields. `HydroPenalties` and `HydroStagePenalties` have identical (name, type) lists — every field is `f64` and every name matches, so the two types are structurally indistinguishable. `HydroPenaltyOverrides` repeats the same 16 names as `Option<f64>`. The cross-crate consequence is visible at `crates/cobre-io/src/resolution/penalties.rs:399-421`, whose own doc line reads `/// Convert a `Hydro`'s entity-level `HydroPenalties` to the per-cell `HydroStagePenalties` — identical fields, distinct types.` followed by a hand-written 16-line positional copy. Because every source and target field is `f64`, transposing two lines there (for example `evaporation_violation_pos_cost` and `evaporation_violation_neg_cost`) compiles and type-checks.

candidates.fixShape: Collapse the two identical structs into one declaration owned by the entity module, and have the resolved per-(hydro, stage) table store that single type rather than a twin. The override struct stays distinct because its `Option` semantics differ, but it should be derived from the same field list rather than restated, so a new penalty column is added once. The hand-written conversion in the cobre-io resolution layer then disappears entirely, taking its silent-transposition hazard with it. If keeping two nominal types is preferred for layering reasons, the replacement guard is a conversion that cannot be written positionally — a `From` impl generated alongside the declaration, plus a test that asserts each of the 16 columns round-trips to a distinct sentinel value so a swap fails loudly.

candidates.title: SystemBuilder enforces canonical order for nine collections and delegates it by doc comment for the seven scenario/stochastic tables it never sorts or checks

evidence.command: grep -n 'sort_canonical(&mut\|sort_by_key(|s| s.id)\|sort_by_key(|c| c.id.0)' crates/cobre-core/src/system/builder.rs; echo ---; grep -n 'self.inflow_models = \|self.load_models = \|self.ncs_models = \|self.inflow_history = \|self.external_scenarios = \|self.external_load_scenarios = \|self.external_ncs_scenarios = ' crates/cobre-core/src/system/builder.rs; echo ---; sed -n '432,434p;438,440p;466,468p' crates/cobre-core/src/system/mod.rs; echo ---; sed -n '158,160p' crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/precompute.rs
evidence.reading: `build` sorts nine collections (seven operational families via `sort_canonical`, plus stages and generic constraints). The seven setters at :230-:299 store their vectors verbatim and `build` never touches them again, yet the accessors at mod.rs:432/438/466 promise 'in canonical order'. The three `*_models` setters state no ordering obligation at all, so the promise appears only on the read side. A consumer already documents the order as a precondition: `PrecomputedPar::build` in cobre-stochastic declares `inflow_models` as 'sorted by (hydro_id, stage_id) from the system'. The producer that actually satisfies it is cobre-io (for example `crates/cobre-io/src/scenarios/estimation.rs:1030 rows.sort_by_key(|r| (r.hydro_id.0, r.stage_id));`), i.e. an L2 crate, so the L0 owner of the declaration-order invariance rule does not own its enforcement for these tables. `with_scenario_models` at mod.rs:572 widens the gap: it replaces `inflow_models` after construction with no sort and no validation, on a type whose own doc calls it 'immutable and thread-safe after construction'.

candidates.fixShape: Make the L0 owner own the invariant it advertises. Either the builder sorts these seven tables into their documented canonical key the way it already sorts the other nine, or it validates them as sorted and returns a validation error otherwise — the second is cheaper and preserves the current cobre-io behaviour byte-for-byte, since cobre-io already emits them sorted. Whichever is chosen, the accessor doc promise and the setter contract must agree, and the post-construction replacement path needs the same treatment as the constructor path rather than being an unchecked hole. The roadmap-consistent end state is different and larger: these seven tables are the Milestone-1 'stochastic off System' set, so the eventual home is the cobre-stochastic store, which owns its own ordering. Until that move lands, the invariant should be enforced where it is declared rather than left as a doc comment.

candidates.title: Two ValidationError variants are constructed nowhere in the workspace and claim an emitter that never imports the type; the parameter that would implement one is dead behind a TODO

evidence.command: grep -rn 'DisconnectedBus\|InvalidPenalty' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '^crates/cobre-core/src/error.rs'; echo ---; grep -rn 'ValidationError' crates/cobre-io/src --include='*.rs' | wc -l; echo ---; sed -n '88,92p' crates/cobre-core/src/topology/network.rs; echo ---; grep -rni 'no connections\|isolated bus\|connectivity' crates/cobre-io/src crates/cobre-sddp/src --include='*.rs' | wc -l
evidence.reading: Outside its own declaration and Display arm, `DisconnectedBus` appears only in a TODO comment and `InvalidPenalty` appears nowhere at all — neither variant is ever constructed in production or test code. Both carry the doc line 'Emitted by `cobre-io` validation' (error.rs:63 and :70), but cobre-io mentions the identifier `ValidationError` zero times, so it cannot emit them. The `NetworkTopology::build` signature takes a `buses: &[Bus]` slice that is immediately discarded via `let _ = buses;` to satisfy the unused-parameter lint, and the rule the TODO points at exists nowhere in cobre-io or cobre-sddp either. The result is an L0 public validation vocabulary advertising a bus-connectivity rule the system does not implement, and a public L0 constructor whose signature promises an input it does not read.

candidates.fixShape: Decide whether the disconnected-bus rule is wanted, then make the code say so. If it is wanted, implement it where the topology is already being built — that is the one place with every entity family in hand — and drop the parameter's discard; the penalty-validity variant needs the same treatment or an owner who actually raises it. If it is not wanted, remove both variants, remove the now-purposeless `buses` parameter from the builder signature, and delete the TODO, so the enum lists only rules the crate enforces. Either way the two stale 'Emitted by cobre-io validation' doc lines must go, because cobre-io does not reference this error type at all and a reader chasing that claim finds nothing. Neither variant is reserved config, so the 'unwired config is reserved, not dead' rule does not shelter them; if the owner intends them as a reserved seam for a future network-validation pass, that intent belongs in the mirror's reserved-seam register where the dismissal can cite it.

candidates.title: The wire-payload reproducibility rule is enforced by three different bespoke mechanisms and skipped for six HashMap fields that serialize inside the same System payload

evidence.command: sed -n '61,66p' crates/cobre-core/src/system/mod.rs; echo '--- mechanism 2 ---'; sed -n '72p' crates/cobre-core/src/model/resolved/generic.rs; echo '--- mechanism 3 ---'; sed -n '701,703p' crates/cobre-core/src/model/scenario.rs; echo '--- unguarded ---'; grep -n 'HashMap' crates/cobre-core/src/model/horizon.rs crates/cobre-core/src/topology/cascade.rs crates/cobre-core/src/topology/network.rs | grep -v 'use std\|::new()\|let mut'
evidence.reading: cobre-core states the same rule three times and enforces it three different ways: `serde(skip)` on the seven index maps with an explicit wire-reproducibility rationale, a hand-written `Serialize` that sorts its composite keys, and a `BTreeMap` chosen over `HashMap` for the correlation profiles. Meanwhile `HorizonGraph`, `CascadeTopology` and `NetworkTopology` each carry `derive(Serialize, Deserialize)` (horizon.rs:21, cascade.rs:19, network.rs:58) and six `HashMap` fields between them, and all three are non-skipped fields of `SystemRepr` (system/mod.rs:157, :158, :161), so they ride the same postcard payload the skip comment is protecting. No live wrong result follows today: the broadcast serializes once on rank 0 and the round-trip guard is a value-equality assertion, not a byte comparison. What is missing is a single owner — the rule has no one statement, no shared mechanism, and nothing that fails when a new nested type serializes a HashMap.

candidates.fixShape: Give the rule one owner instead of three restatements. State once, in the crate root or the system module, that anything reachable from the System payload must serialize in a content-determined order, and satisfy it uniformly — the cheapest route is switching these six fields to an ordered map, since all six are keyed by an already-`Ord` entity id or stage id and none is on a hot path where the lookup cost would matter. The two topology maps additionally have a natural non-map wire form, since their contents are already derived from canonical-ordered entity slices. Whatever mechanism is picked, the guard that keeps it true is a test that serializes two independently-built but equal Systems and compares bytes, which is the assertion the current round-trip test deliberately does not make. If the owner judges byte-level payload reproducibility to be a non-goal, the right fix is the opposite one: retire the skip comment's rationale and the two other bespoke mechanisms, so the crate stops implying a contract it does not keep.

candidates.title: Stage.index encodes the canonical stage order but is assigned in cobre-io and never re-derived or validated by the builder that owns that order

evidence.command: sed -n '283,285p' crates/cobre-core/src/model/temporal.rs; echo '--- builder ---'; sed -n '364p' crates/cobre-core/src/system/builder.rs; echo '--- any index handling in core system module ---'; grep -rn '\.index' crates/cobre-core/src/system/ | grep -v tests | wc -l; echo '--- assignment site ---'; sed -n '811,816p' crates/cobre-io/src/stages.rs
evidence.reading: `Stage.index` is documented as the position in the canonical-ordered stage vector. `SystemBuilder::build` re-sorts the stages into exactly that order at builder.rs:364, but the whole cobre-core system module never reads or writes the field — the grep for `.index` outside tests returns zero hits, and `validate.rs` has no stage-index check alongside its duplicate and cross-reference checks. The only writer is the cobre-io stage parser at stages.rs:811-815. Two crates therefore encode one ordering fact, and the crate that performs the sort is not the crate that records its result. Any other producer reaching `SystemBuilder` — the Python binding, a test fixture, a future engine — can hand in stages whose `index` disagrees with its post-sort slot, and the builder accepts it silently. That the field is a live footgun is already recorded downstream: `crates/cobre-sddp/src/production/hydro_models/production.rs:136-139` warns 'Key by the 0-based study_stages position, NOT stage.index', and stage_key.rs:30-32 documents `StudyPos` as equal to `Stage::index` only when no pre-study stages are declared.

candidates.fixShape: Move the assignment to the sort. The builder already establishes the canonical stage order, so it should reassign each stage's position immediately after sorting, making the field a derived value that cannot disagree with its slot and letting the cobre-io parser drop its own loop. If reassignment is unacceptable because some caller supplies an index with independent meaning, the alternative is a validation pass beside the existing duplicate-stage check that rejects any stage whose recorded index differs from its position, so the disagreement is an error rather than a silent wrong-stage lookup. The stronger long-term shape, given the typed keys already in the temporal module, is to stop storing the position on the stage at all and let callers ask for it through the existing key types, which is the distinction those newtypes were introduced to enforce.

evidence.reading: The flat cell-index invariant is owned once for the thermal table by `thermal_cell_index`, which also carries a debug assertion protecting its stride. For hydro, line, pumping and contract the same arithmetic is written out at 14 separate sites. The precedent is not hypothetical: the thermal family already diverged once, gaining a `n_stages + k_max` stride for delivery-stage padding, and that divergence is exactly what forced the helper into existence. Any second family that needs a different stride must be tracked through 14 call sites with no compile-time guard, in a table whose indexing correctness the solver depends on.

candidates.fixShape: Give the four remaining families the same treatment the thermal table already has: one private index helper per family, or a single shared helper taking the stride, so the layout rule is stated once and each accessor reads a named call rather than repeating the multiply-add. This is a mechanical, behaviour-preserving change confined to one file, and it makes a future stride change for any family a one-line edit instead of a fourteen-site sweep. It also lets the debug assertion that currently guards only the thermal stride be applied uniformly.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-core/src/system/mod.rs:1750 (`fully_populated_system_survives_postcard_roundtrip_intact`) guarding the `SystemRepr` hand-mirror at crates/cobre-core/src/system/mod.rs:147
positives.why: The deserialize-only mirror struct is exactly the hand-maintained duplicate this station usually raises, and it is documented as a silent-corruption hazard ('postcard is non-self-describing, so a reorder silently decodes into the wrong fields'). It is not a candidate, because a named regression test builds a fully populated System across every field and asserts value equality after a postcard round-trip, with a failure comment that names the drift it detects. This is the pattern the other findings in this envelope are missing: a duplicated declaration pinned by a test that says what its failure means.

_needsHuman: Destination for `StageLagTransition`: cobre-stochastic is the only L1 consumer today, but if the future cobre-model carve-out is meant to own multistage layout descriptions then the type may belong there instead, and moving it twice is worse than waiting.

Whether the six HashMap fields nested in the System payload are a deliberate exemption from the wire-reproducibility rationale stated at crates/cobre-core/src/system/mod.rs:62, or an oversight — the answer decides whether the fix is to make them ordered or to retire the rationale.

Whether the disconnected-bus rule is still wanted at all: implementing it may reject decks that load today, so the choice between implementing the variant and deleting it is an owner call, not a cleanup call.

Whether `System::with_scenario_models` is intended as a permanent post-construction mutation seam on an otherwise immutable type, or a temporary bridge for the inflow-estimation pass that the Milestone-1 stochastic-store move is expected to delete.
